function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Decision budget exhausted (call 20 of 20). The red block is still on the table at about x=0.046, y=0.078 and the gripper is empty (measured opening 0.016 = closed on air after four attempts). A grasp needs two more calls and the placement one more, so the task cannot be finished. Not claiming success.", "hindsight": "Camera/frame facts I needed at call 1. (1) SIDE view: horizontal is world x, image-right is +x, about 5.4 px per cm; the black base mount at far right is x about +0.30. (2) FRONT view: horizontal is world y, image-right is -y, about 3.5 px per cm. (3) WRIST view: u is the jaw axis = world y, image-right is -y, about 3.4 normalised units per metre; -x is toward the top. (4) The jaws separate along y but the pads extend only about 2.5 cm either side in x, so a block 5 cm off in x still looks centred in the wrist view and the close catches air. Confirm the x offset in the SIDE view. That mis-diagnosis cost four grasps: all closes were at x=-0.016 while the block was at x=+0.046, whereas my y values 0.075 to 0.088 were correct to within 1 cm. (5) eef_pos is essentially at pad level: table z=0.80, block top z=0.83, so grasp at z about 0.82 to 0.83; at z 0.81 or below the pads jam into the table and the servo loses authority (a 4.5 cm +x command advanced 0.9 cm, joint_eff 24 N m on joint 4). (6) The interpolator sizes each call from the largest normalised delta including the gripper, measured from the current measured state: a pure Cartesian command with an unchanged gripper gets only 2 to 3 control steps, gripper 0.5 retains the previous latch and buys about 40 steps, a full 0 or 1 buys about 80. (7) Measured gripper 0.016 means closed on nothing; a held block reads intermediate. (8) Bowl centre about x=-0.125, y=+0.088, so it was 17 cm from the block almost purely along -x with nearly equal y; a -x sweep with closed pads at z about 0.82 was the viable last-resort push. (9) Spend the first two calls on two orthogonal test translations to fix all three view sign conventions before descending."}
